newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air Transat to start Paris-Montreal flights Nov 1.
newsitem.headline: Air Transat to start Paris-Montreal flights Nov 1.

text.p: Canadian airline Air Transat said it planned to launch scheduled passenger services between Paris and Montreal from November 1.

"We plan to start with two weekly flights on the route from the 1997-98 winter season, using Lockheed TriStar 10-11 and Boeing 757 aircraft, with the possibility of rising to three weekly during the 1998-99 winter season," a Paris-based Air Transat official told Reuters.
The 10-11 will be able to carry about eight tonnes of cargo on the route and the 757, four tonnes.
Earlier this year, the Canadian authorities designated Montreal-based Air Transat as the second scheduled airline operator between Canada and France, the other being state carrier Air Canada.
This followed the withdrawal in autumn 1996 of Canadian Airlines International, which operated a daily service between Paris and Toronto.
Air Transat currently operates passenger-only charter flights between France and Canada on which little if any cargo is carried, said a source at the airline.
The airline has appointed Paris-CDG airport-based Fair Cargo as its French cargo sales agent, with immediate effect.

Before the launch of scheduled services, Fair Cargo's activities on behalf of Air Transat are largely limited to developing off-line capacity via a trucking link to and from with Amsterdam Schiphol airport, a spokesman for the agent said.
